---
title: "What's unusual this week"
subtitle: "Everything a module's own fixed rule flagged, in one list, each item with its label and its evidence"
---

```{python}
from datetime import datetime

import pandas as pd

from pdi import site

items, meta = site.load("unusual", "week")


def _badge(r) -> str:
    return site.finding_badge({"label": r["label"], "reason": r["label_reason"]}, to_root=".")


def _line(r) -> str:
    period = str(r["period"])[:7] if r["rule"] != "price move" else str(r["period"])[:10]
    seen = datetime.fromisoformat(r["first_seen"]).strftime("%-d %b %Y")
    return (f'- {_badge(r)} **{r["module_name"]}.** {r["sentence"]} '
            f'(Refers to {period}; first seen {seen}. Evidence: [page]({r["page"]}), '
            f'[data](data/v1/{r["table"]}).)')
```

Each module flags the moves its own rule calls unusual. This page puts them in one list. Every
rule was fixed before the page was first built, and each is listed at the bottom. A flag says
that something unusual happened. It does not say why, or what comes next.

```{python}
#| output: asis
if items.empty and meta.get("status"):
    print(site.empty_state(meta, "This week's list"))
else:
    built = datetime.fromisoformat(meta["built_at"]).strftime("%-d %B %Y, %H:%M UTC")
    new = items[items["new"]] if len(items) else items
    standing = items[~items["new"]] if len(items) else items
    print(f'Built {built}. {len(items)} items are flagged now; {len(new)} of them were first '
          f'seen in the last {meta["window_days"]} days. Items labelled prediction: '
          f'{meta["predictions"]}.\n')
    print("## New this week\n")
    if meta.get("first_build"):
        print("This is the first build, so nothing can be called new yet: there is no earlier "
              "build to compare with. Everything flagged now is listed below as standing.\n")
    elif new.empty:
        print(f'Nothing new was flagged in the last {meta["window_days"]} days.\n')
    for _, r in new.iterrows():
        print(_line(r))
    print("\n## Still standing\n")
    if standing.empty:
        print("Nothing else is flagged.\n")
    for _, r in standing.iterrows():
        print(_line(r))
```

## The rules

```{python}
#| output: asis
for m in meta.get("modules", []):
    rule = m.get("rule") or "not exported yet"
    status = f' ({m["status"]})' if m.get("status") else ""
    print(f'- **{m["name"]}**, {m["items"]} flagged now{status}: an item is listed when {rule}')
```

An item counts as "new this week" when a build first saw it in the seven days before this one.
The label beside each item is its module's. No item can be labelled a prediction unless its
module's out-of-sample test passed. Each build checks this in code and stops if the check
fails. How the labels are decided is on the [methodology page](methodology.qmd#finding-labels).
